_meta.source: Hand-curated estimates of card acceptance, cash use and ATM tips. Rules for foreign cards change (especially Russia and Belarus): check with your bank.

tips: When a card machine or ATM offers to charge you in your home currency, choose the local currency: the conversion rate is worse.
Carry a second card in case one is blocked, and tell your bank where you are travelling if it requires it.

AL.cashFor: Most small shops, cafés, furgons, guesthouses, and almost everything outside Tirana
AL.atm: Most ATMs charge a fee per withdrawal, so take out larger amounts less often.
AL.note: Some tourist places accept euros, usually at a poor rate.

ME.cashFor: Small cafés, bakeries, markets, buses and private rooms
ME.atm: ATMs often charge a fee per withdrawal.
ME.note: Uses the euro, though not in the EU.

BA.cashFor: Bakeries, markets, small cafés, buses and taxis
BA.atm: ATMs often charge a fee per withdrawal.
BA.note: The convertible mark (KM) is pegged to the euro (€1 ≈ 1.96 KM); some places accept euros.

RS.cashFor: Markets, bakeries, kiosks and some taxis
RS.atm: Some ATMs charge a fee; bank ATMs are usually cheapest.

XK.atm: ATMs often charge a fee per withdrawal.

MK.cashFor: Markets, small shops, buses and taxis
MK.atm: ATMs often charge a fee per withdrawal.

HR.cashFor: Some small cafés, market stalls and private apartments
HR.atm: Avoid Euronet ATMs (high fees and poor rates); bank ATMs are cheaper.

GR.cashFor: Kiosks (periptero), some small tavernas and taxis
GR.atm: Avoid Euronet ATMs (high fees and poor rates); bank ATMs are cheaper.
GR.note: Shops must accept cards by law, but some small places still prefer cash.

BG.cashFor: Small shops, markets, minibuses and some taxis
BG.atm: Avoid Euronet ATMs (high fees and poor rates); bank ATMs are cheaper.

RO.cashFor: Markets, village shops and some guesthouses
RO.atm: Avoid Euronet ATMs (high fees and poor rates); bank ATMs are cheaper.

MD.cashFor: Markets, minibuses, trolleybus conductors, and most places outside Chișinău
MD.atm: ATMs are easy to find in Chișinău; fees vary.

HU.cashFor: Market stalls and some small bars
HU.atm: Avoid Euronet ATMs (high fees and poor rates); bank ATMs are cheaper.

SK.atm: Avoid Euronet ATMs (high fees and poor rates); bank ATMs are cheaper.

CZ.cashFor: Rarely needed: even small pubs take cards
CZ.atm: Avoid Euronet ATMs (high fees and poor rates); bank ATMs are cheaper.

AT.cashFor: Some cafés, bakeries, wine taverns (Heurigen) and market stalls
AT.atm: Bank ATMs are the cheapest; avoid Euronet ATMs.

PL.atm: Avoid Euronet ATMs (high fees and poor rates); bank ATMs are cheaper.
PL.note: BLIK is the local phone-payment system; foreign cards and Apple/Google Pay work everywhere.

EE.cashFor: Rarely needed: Estonia is almost cashless

RU.cashFor: Everything: Visa and Mastercard cards issued abroad do not work in Russia
RU.atm: Foreign cards do not work at ATMs. Bring euros or US dollars and exchange them at banks.
RU.note: Rules change often; check before you go whether any card from your country works (e.g. some UnionPay or Mir cards).

UA.cashFor: Little: cards and phone payments are everywhere

BY.atm: Check with your bank whether payments in Belarus are blocked.
BY.note: Some foreign banks block card payments in Belarus because of sanctions.

TW.cashFor: Night markets, small restaurants and local shops; an EasyCard covers transport and convenience stores
TW.atm: ATMs in 7-Eleven and banks accept foreign cards; fees vary by bank.
TW.note: Local apps (LINE Pay, JKOPAY) are common; Apple/Google Pay works in convenience stores and chains.

JP.cashFor: Some small restaurants, temples, shrines and rural shops
JP.atm: 7-Eleven (Seven Bank) and Japan Post ATMs accept foreign cards.
JP.note: You can add a Suica card to an iPhone and pay with it almost everywhere.

TH.cashFor: Street food, markets, tuk-tuks and small guesthouses
TH.atm: Thai ATMs charge foreign cards a fee (about 220 THB) per withdrawal: take out larger amounts.

VN.cashFor: Street food, markets, small hotels and motorbike taxis
VN.atm: Some ATMs charge fees and many have low withdrawal limits.
VN.note: Prices have many zeros: check notes carefully (10,000 and 100,000 look alike).

MY.atm: Bank ATMs are easy to find.

SG.cashFor: A few hawker stalls (most take cards or PayNow now)

KH.cashFor: Most things: prices are often in US dollars, with change in riel
KH.atm: ATMs give US dollars; most charge about $4–6 per withdrawal.
KH.note: Bring clean, untorn US dollar notes: damaged ones are often refused.

theth.note: Cash only: bring enough from Shkodër, as there are no ATMs.

zabljak.note: Few places take cards; there are only a couple of ATMs.
